recentItems.title: US Ambassador to Turkiye: Iran war’s unintended consequences | Talk to Al Jazeera
recentItems.description:
The United States ambassador to Turkiye and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq says Washington’s relationship with the countries in the Middle East needs to change.

Tom Barrack says the US no longer seeks to dominate the region.

He won’t say whether the war in Iran was a mistake – but acknowledges the instability it caused has led to unintended consequences.

Barrack says President Donald Trump is against what he calls "forever wars", and ending the US-Israel war on Iran will require a major compromise. According to him, each side will have to accept conditions it does not like.

However, he is worried that growing tensions could lead to miscalculation.

Barrack says trust is lacking between Washington and Tehran, and that is hampering talks to agree on a deal.

He tells Al Jazeera that countries in the region should not depend on the US to solve their problems and that they need to look out for themselves. He insists the Trump administration has not abandoned the region, but is rather re-examining its role.

Barrack admits that years of US involvement in the region demonstrate that intervention and regime change do not work. He says it is time to put down the guns and resolve disputes through negotiations and mutual respect.

recentItems.title: Iraq frees families held over suspected ISIL ties as old wounds reopen
recentItems.description:
Ten years after the battle of Mosul began, Iraq is still grappling with aftermath of ISIL’s crimes.
Many families of people suspected of having links to the armed group have spent years in what the government calls “rehabilitation camps”.
Now they are being released, but their reintegration is reopening old wounds.

Al Jazeera’s Peter Smith reports from inside the Jed’ah camp near Mosul, Iraq.

recentItems.title: Strait of Hormuz near ‘maximum danger’ as US-Iran diplomacy stalls, analyst says
recentItems.description:
Diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict appear to be stalling.
President Donald Trump says the US is not negotiating with Iran.
Speaking at Joint Base Andrews, he was vague about potential further military action before the US midterm elections next month. 

Iran's senior negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has held talks with the Supreme Leader about the war with the US. That's according to state media.
The two also discussed the economic sanctions imposed by Washington. 

Alexandru Hudisteanu, a military defence analyst specialising in maritime security, tells Al Jazeera the Strait of Hormuz is near “maximum level of danger” as US-Iran diplomacy stalls. He warns further escalation could threaten shipping and drive fuel prices higher.
